language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hola! My name is Maria. Welcome to La Cantina, my grandmother's diner, where I work as a flamenco dancer.
Every weekend I dance in a flamengo show here! Dancing is fun, but it is also physically hard work!
When I am dancing, I feel my muscles stretch and my joints move.
My heart and lungs work faster to provide oxygen to my body.
Afterwards I get very hungry!
As a dancer, I know that all the different parts of my body, from the smallest to largest, work together to keep me healthy.
Vamos, let's go learn more about the body systems!
Come on, let's join Maria as she learns about the body systems.

When I am dancing, I feel my muscles stretch and my joints move.
My heart and lungs work faster to provide oxygen to my body.
Afterwards I get very hungry!
As a dancer, I know that all the different parts of my body, from the smallest to largest, work together to keep me healthy.
Vamos, let's go learn more about the body systems!
Come on, let's join Maria as she learns about the body systems.
We humans, and all other living things are made up of many smaller parts.

The smallest unit of a living being
is a cell.
A collection of the same type of cells is a tissue. Tissues make up organs, like our brain or our heart.

A group of organs working together to perform a process is called a
body system.
Everything together is called an organism. That's a lot to take in I guess.
Let's practise! Can you put these units in order from smallest to largest?

Let's practise by answering the following questions.
Click the right answer.
Thanks! Now I know more about the different systems responsible for each of these processes.
Muscles contract and relax when I'm dancing.

Some muscles, like the leg's hamstring and quadriceps, work in pairs to
move bones.
Skeletal joints are also important. Hinge joints can only bend and straighten, whereas, the ball and socket joints allow more movement.
Not all muscles work with bones. The heart has muscles that are not attached to bones.

The brain sends and receives information through the spinal cord and nerves.
The nervous system is similar to a telephone network.

It sends information through lines:
the nerve.
Information can come from the brain, for example, when the brain tells your feet to move.
Information can also go to the brain, for example, when you taste something bad, your mouth tells your brain "Yuck."
